title: Virtual GPU lanes and rate contracts for Dedicated capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define and implement a virtual lane abstraction for Dedicated GPU pools that enforces per-tenant throughput contracts (rate contracts) and enables graceful degradation when physical GPU capacity is constrained. Deliverables include runtime lane enforcement, autoscale interplay rules, quota enforcement API, and a rollout plan for existing Dedicated customers.
background: Customers on Dedicated ask for predictable throughput guarantees without rigid hard-slicing of GPUs. Current approaches either hard-slice (wasteful) or oversubscribe (noisy neighbor issues). We need a middle-ground: virtual lanes that provide strong statistical throughput guarantees with soft preemption and controlled fairness so tenants hit SLOs while cluster utilization remains high.
goals: Provide per-tenant throughput contracts measured in token/sec and concurrent request budget
Enforce contracts via virtual GPU lanes that can be moved across physical GPUs without service interruption
Integrate with autoscaling so lane quality is maintained during scale events
Offer quota enforcement API for admin and customer visibility
Minimize noisy neighbor amplification and provide clear fallbacks when capacity is insufficient
non_goals: Full hw-level GPU partitioning (no changes to GPU drivers)
Replacing Dedicated hard reservations for customers who require strict isolation
Implementing model-specific kernel changes — focus is scheduling and admission control
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can create/delete virtual lanes mapped to physical GPU pools
Per-lane enforcement maintains >=90% of contracted throughput for best-effort 95th percentile workload patterns
Soft preemption reduces tail latency impact on priority lanes by 50% during contention scenarios compared to baseline oversubscribe strategy
Autoscaler honors lane SLAs: when autoscale triggered, lanes are redistributed within 30s and contracts are rebalanced without request loss
Admin API exposes current lane allocations, consumed throughput, queued requests, and enforced quotas
E2E test harness reproduces noisy neighbor scenarios and validates degradation policies
technical_design: We will implement a lightweight lane manager in the Serving Control Plane and a per-node lane enforcer in the inference agent. Lanes are logical objects with attributes: lane_id, tenant_id, token_rate_limit, concurrency_limit, priority_class, eviction_policy. The node enforcer maps lanes to GPU partitions via scheduler slots and maintains a per-lane token bucket for admission. Admission decisions are made at request enqueue time. Soft preemption is implemented by a two-step mechanism: 1) admission denial and queueing based on token bucket; 2) cooperative eviction signals that reduce existing request slot allocations for low-priority lanes (deferred by Fay backoff) to free slots for higher-priority lanes. Autoscaler integration: scaling events trigger lane rebalance plans computed centrally, using a stable mapping algorithm to minimize lane migrations (prefer delta relocation under 20% of lanes). Metrics and traces will be emitted: lane.allocated_tokens_per_sec, lane.consumed_tokens_per_sec, lane.queue_depth, lane.preemptions, lane.migrations. Config knobs: per-tenant burst_window_seconds, emergency_eviction_threshold, migration_grace_period_seconds.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Soft preemption chosen over hard preemption to avoid request loss and to maintain model cache locality
We will not attempt driver-level GPU partitioning to avoid vendor lock-in and driver complexity
Favor fast, cooperative eviction over heavy-weight checkpointing for in-flight requests to reduce implementation time
Expose conservative default rate limits and allow customers to opt into aggressive performance modes
risks: Unintended tail latency regressions if cooperative eviction oscillates
Inefficient packing when tenants have highly spiky traffic, reducing utilization
Complex autoscaler interactions could cause repeated migrations if thresholds are not tuned
Customer confusion between Dedicated hard reservations and virtual lane guarantees — needs clear docs and SLAs
mitigations: Start with a pilot on a subset of fleets and high-touch customers
Implement hysteresis and rate-limited migration decisions to prevent oscillation
Provide conservative defaults that favor predictability over utilization initially
Run canary experiments with synthetic spike workloads and real customer traffic patterns
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal test fleet implementation and unit/integration tests (4 weeks). Phase 2: Pilot with 3 Dedicated customers, opt-in only, monitor metrics and logs (6 weeks). Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 25% of Dedicated clusters with opt-in billing adjustments and updated docs (8 weeks). Phase 4: GA with defaults and UI controls in Console (support for editing lane contracts and viewing real-time usage). Each phase gated by SLO and stability checks.
testing_plan: Create e2e scenarios: steady-state high throughput, sudden spikes, long-tail requests, mixed-priority tenants. Use synthetic job generator to reproduce noisy neighbor patterns at different burstiness. Add fuzz tests for migration and failure modes. Load tests measuring token/sec, tail latency, and migration count. Integrate tests into CI and scheduled nightly chaos runs.
monitoring_and_alerting: New alerts: lane_contract_breach (>=1 lane violating contract for >1m), lane_migration_failures (>3 failed migrations in 10m), lane_preemption_rate_spike (sustained preemptions > threshold). Dashboards: per-cluster lane utilization heatmap, top violating tenants, migration patterns over time, latency vs contract utilization. Add tracing hooks to link API request IDs to lane enforcement decisions for post-mortem.
api_spec: POST /v1/dedicated/lanes -> create lane with tenant_id, token_rate_limit, concurrency_limit, priority_class. GET /v1/dedicated/lanes?tenant_id= -> list lanes. PATCH /v1/dedicated/lanes/{lane_id} -> update contract. GET /v1/dedicated/lanes/{lane_id}/metrics -> timeseries of allocated vs consumed tokens. Admin endpoint: POST /v1/admin/lanes/{lane_id}/evict -> force-evict lane (support only for emergency ops). All endpoints respect RBAC and produce audit log entries.
observability_notes: Emit structured logs with fields: lane_id, tenant_id, decision, reason, token_granted, queue_depth, node_id. Instruments must be low-overhead and sampled for high-frequency events. Ensure logs are scrubbed for PII. Add synthetic SLA tests that run each 5m and feed metrics into alerts if degradation > predefined thresholds.
docs_and_customer_communication: Write Console pages explaining 'Virtual Lanes' vs 'Reserved Capacity'. Update billing docs to describe guaranteed vs best-effort tiers and opt-in pricing. Prepare FAQ and recommended configs for common workload patterns: chat, completion-heavy, and long-context evals. Coordinate with Solutions and Sales for pilot invite messaging.
open_questions: What default token_rate units should we expose for customers (tokens/sec vs requests/sec)?
How should burst credits be priced and represented in Console?
What migration grace period provides acceptable balance between SLA adherence and migration overhead?
updates: 2025-11-10: Initial design review with Runtime team; agreed on token-bucket admission at agent level.
2025-12-02: POC lane manager implemented in staging; basic create/list/delete flows working.
2026-01-15: Benchmarks showed 12% improvement in 95th p99 latency for priority lanes vs oversubscribe baseline in steady load tests.
2026-02-05: Discovered oscillation during autoscaler stress test; added migration hysteresis and backoff plan.
2026-03-01: Pilot customers identified (3) and NDA/opt-in materials drafted; security review started.
2026-03-10: Pilot rollout scheduled for 2026-03-20 pending final canary metrics and operational runbook completion.
